answer: A network can resist fake identities by checking where each agent really sits. Independent landmarks send unpredictable timing challenges, and an agent must answer fast enough to match its claimed location, as if proving it is moored at one wharf rather than everywhere at once. Copies run by one operator from one machine show almost identical delays, so they cluster and only one survives, like vines pretending to be separate plants on the same trellis. Keeping extra identities means placing real machines in different places, each on its own ledge, and paying that cost again for every fake.
